hamate bone: Medial bone of the distal row; the hook on its palmar surface forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal and the medial boundary of the carpal tunnel.
handle of malleus: Handle of the malleus; embedded in the eardrum, its tip forms the umbo. Tensor tympani attaches here.
head of femur: Rounded articular head of the femur; forms the hip joint with the acetabulum, and its blood supply comes from the medial circumflex femoral artery.
head of fibula: Upper end of the fibula; the common fibular nerve winds around it behind and laterally.
head of humerus: Hemispherical articular head; forms the shoulder joint with the glenoid cavity.
head of malleus: Head of the malleus in the upper middle ear; articulates with the incus.
head of metatarsal bone: Distal head of a metatarsal; bears weight in the sole and articulates with the proximal phalanx.
head of radius: Disc-shaped upper end of the radius; it rotates at the elbow and in children can slip out of the annular ligament.
head of rib: Head of the rib that articulates with the vertebral column.
head of talus: Head articulating with the navicular; the keystone of the medial arch.
head of ulna: Head at the lower end of the ulna; felt on the posteromedial side of the wrist.
hip bone: Large irregular bone formed by the fusion of ilium, ischium and pubis at the acetabulum; with the sacrum it forms the pelvic ring and with the femoral head the hip joint.
hook of hamate bone: Hook of the hamate projecting towards the palm; forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal and can fracture in golfers.
humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris
Head arising from the lateral epicondyle.
humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris
Arises from the medial epicondyle; the ulnar nerve enters the forearm through the arch between the two heads (cubital tunnel).
humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su: Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum superficialis
Arises from the medial epicondyle and the coronoid process.
humerus: The single long bone of the arm; its head forms the shoulder joint with the glenoid cavity of the scapula. The surgical neck (axillary nerve), radial groove (radial nerve) and medial epicondyle (ulnar nerve) matter in fractures because of nerve injury.
hyoglossus muscle: Quadrilateral muscle from the hyoid to the side of the tongue; depresses the tongue. The hypoglossal and lingual nerves run on its surface and the lingual artery deep to it.
hyoid bone: U-shaped bone in the neck at the level of C3 that articulates with no other bone; it gives attachment to the muscles of the tongue and larynx. Its fracture is of forensic importance in strangulation.
hypoglossal canal: Canal above the condyle; the hypoglossal nerve leaves the skull through it.
hypophysial fossa: Fossa in the sella turcica; the pituitary gland lies in it.
iliac crest: Upper border of the ilium; the abdominal and back muscles attach to it, and bone marrow aspiration can be performed here.
iliac fossa: Broad fossa on the inner surface of the ilium; iliacus arises here.
iliac tubercle: Prominence on the outer lip of the iliac crest, about 5 cm behind the ASIS.
iliac tuberosity: Rough area above the auricular surface; the strong sacroiliac ligaments attach to it.
iliacus muscle: Muscle filling the iliac fossa; it joins psoas to insert into the lesser trochanter. Femoral nerve.
iliococcygeus muscle: Thin posterior part of levator ani running from the tendinous arch to the coccyx.
iliocostalis colli muscle: Part of the iliocostalis column running from the upper ribs to the lower cervical vertebrae.
iliocostalis lumborum muscle: Lumbar part of the most lateral column of erector spinae; extends the spine and bends it sideways. Posterior rami of the spinal nerves.
iliocostalis thoracis muscle: Part of the iliocostalis column running from the lower ribs to the upper ribs.
iliolumbar ligament: Strong ligament binding the transverse process of L5 to the iliac crest; stabilises the lumbosacral junction.
iliopectineal arch: Fascial thickening dividing the space between the inguinal ligament and the pubis into muscular (lacuna musculorum) and vascular (lacuna vasorum) compartments.
iliopsoas fascia: Fascia enclosing the iliacus and psoas muscles; a psoas abscess tracks down to the groin within this sheath.
iliopsoas muscle: Psoas major and iliacus joined by a common insertion into the lesser trochanter; the most powerful flexor of the hip.
iliopubic eminence: Prominence where the ilium and pubis meet.
iliotibial tract: Lateral thickening of the fascia lata running from the iliac crest to Gerdy's tubercle of the tibia. In runners it causes a friction syndrome over the lateral femoral condyle.
ilium: The largest, upper part of the hip bone.
impression for costoclavicular ligament: Rough area on the lower surface of the medial end; the costoclavicular ligament to the 1st rib attaches here.
incus: The middle of the three ossicles of the middle ear; it transmits vibration between the malleus and the stapes.
inferior angle of scapula: Lower tip of the scapula; at the level of T7.
inferior articular facet of vertebra: Surface of the inferior articular process that forms a facet joint with the vertebra below.
inferior articular surface of atlas: Lower surface of the lateral mass; forms the lateral atlanto-axial joint with the axis.
inferior articular surface of tibia: Lower surface forming the ankle joint with the talus.
inferior costal facet: Half facet on the lower border of a thoracic vertebral body; articulates with the head of the rib below.
inferior extensor retinaculum of ankle: Y-shaped band on the dorsum of the foot; the deep fibular nerve can be compressed beneath it (anterior tarsal tunnel).
inferior fibular retinaculum: Band holding the fibular tendons on the lateral surface of the calcaneus.
inferior gemellus muscle: Runs from the ischial tuberosity to join the obturator internus tendon; a lateral rotator.
inferior glenohumeral ligament: The most important static stabiliser of the shoulder; prevents anterior dislocation when the arm is abducted and externally rotated.
inferior gluteal line: Lower line on the outer surface of the ilium; bounds the origin of gluteus minimus.
inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscl: Runs from the lateral plate to the neck of the condyle; the only muscle of mastication that starts mouth opening and protrudes the jaw.
inferior horn of thyroid cartilage: Lower extension of the thyroid cartilage; it articulates with the cricoid and allows the tilting that adjusts the pitch of the voice.
inferior mental spine: Lower spine on the inner surface; geniohyoid attaches to it.
inferior nasal concha bone: Independent thin bone attached to the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus beneath it.
inferior nuchal line: Lower line where neck muscles attach; the suboccipital muscles attach to it.
inferior oblique muscle: The only eye muscle arising from the front of the orbital floor; turns the eye up and out and rotates it outwards. Oculomotor nerve.
inferior pharyngeal constrictor: Arises from the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; its cricopharyngeal part is the upper oesophageal sphincter. A Zenker's diverticulum develops in the weak area between its two parts.
inferior pubic ligament: Thick ligament arching beneath the symphysis (arcuate pubic ligament); it rounds off the pubic arch.
